# `operation-removed-after-deprecation`

Operation removed after the deprecation period

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` |
| **Rule IDs** | `operation-removed-after-deprecation` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M6) |
| **Group** | Paths and operations ([RULES.md section 2](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

An operation was removed after it had been deprecated for the configured period, or after its sunset date.

## Why this default

Clients were warned for the agreed period, so the removal follows the API lifecycle.

## Example

From test case [`operation-removed-after-deprecation`](../../test/cases/operation-removed-after-deprecation/): Deprecated on 2026-06-01, removed 173 days later (as of 2026-11-21): past the 90-day period, so the removal is info.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          '200':
            description: ok
-   /pets/{id}:
-     delete:
-       operationId: deletePet
-       deprecated: true
-       x-deprecated-since: 2026-06-01
-       responses:
-         '200':
-           description: ok
  components:
    schemas:
```

Findings:

- `operation-removed-after-deprecation` · info · DELETE /pets/{id}

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  operation-removed-after-deprecation: info
```

## How to fix

Nothing to fix; make sure the removal is in the changelog.
